transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you to the clinic today?

For months now I’ve had this constant heavy, sad feeling that I just can’t seem to shake, even when I’m doing things I used to enjoy. My doctor noticed I wasn't quite myself during a recent check-up and suggested I speak with someone, so that's why I'm here today.
Have you had similar episodes of depression like this before, or is this the first time it has happened?

No, I’ve never felt like this before; this is the first time in my life I've experienced anything of this sort. It is a completely new and unfamiliar feeling for me, and it has been quite disorienting.
How much has this depression affected your daily life and ability to function at work, home, or with self-care? Have you had periods of feeling slowed down or unable to do even simple tasks?

I'm retired, but this has really disrupted my daily life; I've let my intergenerational art circle stall out and keep canceling plans with my friends. I'm also struggling to manage my sister's medical appointments and paperwork because I feel constantly drained, making day-to-day tasks feel like a heavy struggle.
Have you had to stay in bed or been unable to do most daily activities because of this depression, or are you still able to manage basic self-care and get through the day?

I’m not completely bedridden and I can still manage basic self-care, but my daily functioning has definitely suffered. Because I feel so low and drained, I’ve let my intergenerational art circle stall out and keep canceling plans with my friends. I also struggle to keep up with managing my sister’s medical appointments and paperwork, which makes day-to-day life feel much harder to manage.
Over the past few months, have you also had symptoms like poor concentration, changes in sleep or appetite, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or thoughts that life is not worth living?

Yes, I've been waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning with my mind churning, constantly feeling guilty that I'm failing everyone in my life. I haven't noticed much change in my appetite, but on my darkest days, I do sometimes think it would be a relief if I just didn't wake up, though I have no plans to hurt myself.
How much have these symptoms interfered with your ability to function day to day—would you say they cause only some difficulty, or do they make it very hard to carry out your usual activities?

They make it quite hard to manage my day-to-day life. I've had to let my art circle stall out, I keep canceling plans with friends, and keeping up with my sister's medical appointments and paperwork has become a real struggle.
Have these symptoms made it impossible for you to do most of your usual activities, or are you still able to carry on with them even though it is difficult?

It isn't completely impossible, but I've had to let many of my usual activities slide. I've let my art circle stall completely and frequently cancel social plans, though I still occasionally force myself to go to my walking or watercolor clubs with immense effort. Managing my sister's appointments and paperwork from afar has also become very difficult to keep up with.
Would you say these symptoms have made it very difficult to carry out most of your usual activities, or are they still manageable with only some difficulty?

I would say they have made things very difficult rather than just mildly challenging. I've had to let my intergenerational art circle stall, I constantly cancel social plans, and I struggle to manage my sister's appointments and paperwork. It has made day-to-day life feel very hard to manage.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or of ending your life, even if you would not act on them?

I don’t have any plan to hurt myself, but on my lowest days, I do find myself thinking that if I just didn’t wake up, it would be a relief. It sometimes feels like that would just make things simpler for everyone else.
Do these symptoms make it impossible for you to do most of your usual activities or take care of yourself, or are you still able to manage them even though it is very difficult?

I am still able to manage basic self-care, so it is not completely impossible, but it is extremely difficult. Because I feel so low and drained, I've had to let my art circle stall, I keep skipping social plans, and I really struggle to keep up with my sister's appointments and paperwork.
Would you say your depression has made it impossible to do most of your usual activities, or are you still able to carry them out even though it is very difficult?

It isn't completely impossible, but carrying out my usual activities has become extremely difficult. I've let my art circle stall completely and frequently skip my watercolor and walking clubs, though I still try to push myself to go through the motions when I can. Managing my sister's medical paperwork has also become a massive struggle.
Over the past few months, have you been able to do almost none of your usual activities because of the depression, or can you still do most things even though it is very difficult?

It’s really a mix of both, as I haven't stopped everything but have had to let major activities like my art circle stall and frequently cancel social plans. For the things I still manage to do, like occasional watercolor groups or my sister's paperwork, I have to heavily force myself and it feels incredibly difficult and draining.

During the worst part of this depression, have you felt so slowed down, exhausted, or unable to function that you could do almost nothing for most of the day, or are you still able to get through most activities with effort?

I’m not completely bedridden or unable to do anything at all, but it takes immense effort just to get through the day. While I've had to let things slip, like stalling my art circle and canceling social plans, I still force myself to go through the motions of daily life and manage my sister's care. It just leaves me feeling incredibly drained and fatigued.
During your worst days, do you feel so slowed down or exhausted that you can do almost nothing, or are you still able to get through most activities with a lot of effort?

Even on my worst days, I am still able to get through things, but it requires an immense amount of effort and leaves me feeling incredibly drained. I mostly just force myself to go through the motions, though I've had to let some things slide like canceling social plans and letting my art circle stall. I am not completely inactive, but everything just takes so much out of me.
During the worst part of this depression, have you been unable to do almost any of your usual activities for most of the day, or are you still able to do some activities with a lot of effort?

It’s really a mix of both, as I still force myself to do some things like occasionally attending my watercolor group or walking club, but it takes immense effort just to push myself out the door and go through the motions. At the same time, other activities have completely fallen by the wayside, like letting my intergenerational art circle stall out and constantly canceling social plans because I feel too drained.
During your worst days, do you feel so slowed down or unable to function that you can do almost nothing for most of the day, or are you still able to do some activities with a lot of effort?

I'm not completely bedridden, but doing anything on those days requires an immense amount of effort to just push myself and go through the motions. Because of how drained I feel, I've had to let major things slide like letting my art circle stall, and I struggle heavily to keep up with my sister's paperwork and appointments.

During the past few months, have there been days when your depression made it almost impossible to do most activities or even get out of bed, or have you generally still been able to do most things with a lot of effort?

I haven't been completely bedridden, but I have to force myself and put in a massive amount of effort just to go through the motions of daily life. I've had to push myself out the door for basic things, while letting my intergenerational art circle stall and struggling to keep up with my sister's appointments and paperwork.

I'm not completely unable to do anything, but it takes an immense amount of effort to do almost anything. I have to force myself to go through the motions, and because it's so exhausting, I've let things slide like letting my art circle stall, canceling social plans, and struggling to keep up with my sister's paperwork.

At the same time, some things have become too difficult to maintain, so I've let my art circle stall out, canceled social plans, and struggled to keep up with my sister's paperwork.

It’s really a mix of both, as I have forced myself with immense effort to go through the motions for certain tasks, like managing my sister’s appointments or occasionally going to my watercolor group. However, there are major parts of my routine that I simply couldn't keep up with at all, such as letting my art circle stall completely and frequently canceling plans with my friends.

During the worst part of this depression, were you so slowed down or unable to function that you could do almost nothing for most of the day, or were you still able to do most activities even though it took a lot of effort?

I haven't been completely unable to do anything, but carrying out any task takes an immense amount of effort. I constantly have to push myself just to go through the motions, which is why I've let my art circle stall, canceled social plans, and struggled to keep up with my sister's paperwork.
Have you felt so slowed down or exhausted that you can barely do anything for most of the day, or are you still able to do most activities with a lot of effort?

I feel incredibly low, drained, and fatigued, but I am not completely bedridden and still push myself tremendously just to go through the motions. Because of this exhaustion, I have had to cancel social plans and let my art circle stall. I also struggle constantly to keep up with my sister's medical appointments and paperwork.

I am still trying to do things, but it requires an immense amount of effort. I have to force myself out the door just to go through the motions of my usual activities like the walking club or watercolor group. I feel so drained that I've had to cancel plans and let my art circle stall because keeping up with everything has become such a struggle.

Even on my worst days, I still feel incredibly low and exhausted, but I am generally able to do things if I push myself hard enough. I have to force myself out the door just to go through the motions, though I've ended up canceling many social plans and really struggle to keep up with my sister's paperwork.

Symptoms cause clear social and role impairment, but the patient remains able to perform basic self-care and some activities with effort, which fits a moderate depressive episode rather than mild or severe without psychotic symptoms.
